summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for evaluation of recurrent presyncope and a recent syncopal episode, following progressive dyspnea on exertion. He has a history of end-stage liver disease, cirrhosis, and portal hypertension, and is on the transplant list. Initial workup ruled out pulmonary embolism and acute cardiac ischemia. Echocardiography revealed worsening pulmonary hypertension, confirmed by right heart catheterization, with a mean pulmonary artery pressure of 45 mmHg that increased in the upright position. The findings support a diagnosis of portopulmonary syndrome. He was started on nighttime oxygen therapy due to nocturnal desaturation and prescribed sildenafil, pending insurance approval. His chronic leg weakness was assessed and attributed to deconditioning, with no new neurological pathology. He remained stable, with optimized management of his liver disease and supportive medications. He was discharged home with a plan for follow-up in pulmonary clinic, initiation of home oxygen, and completion of a sleep study to evaluate for obstructive sleep apnea.
